To sync rules, keep GodViewer running in the background before you edit views in a target app.
Get GodViewer working in a few steps
Root your device and install a working LSPosed (or compatible Xposed) framework. Reboot after installation.
Open LSPosed → Modules → enable GodViewer. You only need to scope the target apps you want to edit — the host app itself does not need to be in scope.
Add the apps you want to inspect to the module scope, then force-stop those apps (or reboot) so hooks load cleanly.

Open a scoped app, pull down the notification shade, and use the edit-mode entry (default: the target app\'s notification; optional: GodViewer host notification in Settings): Enable / Undo / Manage Rules. Then tap a view, adjust size / margin / padding / visibility / text / image, and Apply. Rules are saved inside the target app and replay after restart.

• Default entry is the target app notification. If the target app does not request notification permission, choose the host notification entry (Settings → Edit-mode entry).
• Host entry mode: keep GodViewer alive in the background so it can control the last foreground target.
• Synced rules on the Rules tab are read-only mirrors pushed when a target saves rules.
• Corrupt rule files are ignored safely and will not crash the target app.
If the target app does not request notification permission, choose the host notification entry. Once your rules are final, choose \"No notification\" to hide the entry

GodViewer changelog

4.3.6
• Rule pages can now manage rules: open an app and delete a rule, hide or show its view, rewrite its text, or restore the original values. The list also supports multi-select, so several rules can be deleted at once
• Rule management crosses process boundaries and is best effort (still a work in progress): when the target app is running, edits apply right away and the list thumbnail is retaken so you can see the result; otherwise the edits are queued and applied the next time you open that app, with a hint showing how many are waiting
• Hidden rules keep the picture taken before hiding, since a hidden view cannot be captured
• Managing a rule never downgrades an imported one: rules restored from another device keep matching by resource id or text instead of by position
• Fixed: on some devices tapping “Manage rules” on the notification did nothing. The rule manager now opens once you are back inside the app

4.3.5
• Rule backup and restore ships as a work in progress: when the layout differs from the source device, some rules may not apply, thumbnails may be missing, and a rule may latch onto a neighbouring control - refinement continues. If a restore hides the wrong control, use Undo last restore to roll it back
• Rule backup and restore: export every mirrored app's rules to a ZIP file from the rules page (thumbnails stored as-is inside), then restore it after switching phones or reinstalling
• Restore merges by rule key and keeps the newer copy; rules for apps that are not installed are kept and apply on their first launch
• Restored rules apply immediately when the target app is already running, otherwise on its next launch
• Thumbnail sync now runs in batches: apps with many rules no longer lose the tail of their thumbnails, and missing ones backfill as you keep using the app
• Restored rules are matched by resource id or text instead of by position, so a rule from another phone can no longer hide a different control here
• Restored rules now carry their thumbnails over, and hidden or absent controls still show the picture taken on the original device
• Added “Undo last restore” on the rules page: one tap removes every rule from the last restore

4.3.4
• New “God mode” Quick Settings tile (a plain 1x1 tile): one tap hides the edit-mode entry, another restores it (add it from Settings, Android 7.0 and later)
• Turning the tile on also enters edit mode in the last target app - turn it off in Settings
• Hiding the entry now exits edit mode in every running target app, so touch interception cannot linger

4.3.3
• New “no notification” entry mode: once the rules are final, hide the edit-mode entry notification (the GodViewer host notification and the in-app one) — saved rules keep applying
• Hide is the first notification action: it hides the entry and exits edit mode; turn the entry back on in Settings
• Tap the notification to toggle edit mode
• The notification text shows the current mode and what a tap will do

4.3.2
• New host-notification entry for target apps without notification permission (switchable in Settings)
• Live highlight of the selected view
• Batch rule editing: select all / multi-select and batch delete; view thumbnails in the rule list
• In-app update check and copy / clear diagnostic logs
• Rewritten touch interception fixes taps in some hooked apps; smaller click bounds for finer control
• Rewritten dialog style with less dependence on target app code
• New hook approach (migrated to libxposed API 102) for better stability
• Bug fixes and support for more common apps

3.3.2
• Move edit-mode entry to GodViewer host notification (enable / undo / manage rules); targets no longer need notification permission
• More stable edit intercept via Activity touch dispatch + force-clickable refresh
• Clear stale target when reopening the host app
• Isolate injected dialogs from target themes; unify palette with host UI; fix advanced editor blank content

3.2.2
• Donate page with WeChat Pay and Alipay QR codes
• Align secondary page toolbars with primary tab titles

3.2.1 — New UI version
• Host bottom navigation: Home / Guide / Rules / Settings
• Rule mirror list with app icons and detail pages
• Settings: language (system/zh/en), hide desktop icon, check updates, auto-update preference, changelog, user agreement
• Global watermark and tab fade animation

2.2.1
• Cap preview image height so edit buttons stay visible for large views

2.2.0
• Rule manager in the injected UI
• Persist and replay view rules after app restart
